title: Suffering of Christ
definition: The suffering of Christ refers to the physical, emotional, relational, and spiritual agony He endured in obedience to the Father for the salvation of sinners.
summary: Jesus suffered willingly to redeem His people.
christFocus: Christ's suffering reveals His love, obedience, sympathy, and saving purpose.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Christ suffered rejection, temptation, betrayal, mockery, injustice, physical agony, and death. His suffering was real, not symbolic.

He suffered as the righteous One for the unrighteous. His suffering was not accidental tragedy; it was part of God's saving purpose.

Because Christ suffered, He is able to sympathize with His people and sustain them in their own suffering.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Suffering people often wonder whether God understands pain. The suffering of Christ matters because the Savior entered suffering and transformed it into the path of redemption.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring suffering to Christ. Look to His cross for mercy, His sympathy for comfort, and His endurance for strength.
